$comment: Invariant ids the P1 `p1-grading` task owns. The integrate task merges this into docs/invariants-owned.json, which is what `pnpm test:coverage-map` reads. Split per task so two implementers cannot collide on one file. INV-GRD-09 is deliberately absent: it is a rendered-input contract (autocorrect off, spellcheck off, smart punctuation off) and belongs to the player, not to packages/core.

integrate.$comment: Work the integrate task must do that is OUTSIDE this task's file lane (packages/core/src/grading/**, docs/owned/grading.json). Recorded here because a green run cannot see any of it.

required_edits.why: packages/core/src/index.ts exports day/civil, day/streak, ceremony/commit and db/index only. Without this line the grader is unreachable from @freelingo/core: nothing outside packages/core can import it, and every test in this task passes anyway because they all import by relative path.
`pnpm test:coverage-map` reads invariants-owned.json, not this file.

decisions.subject: packages/core/src/grading/packs/** (the es/ja/de grading FIXTURES)
decisions.decision: kept OFF the engine's public surface
decisions.detail: grading/index.ts no longer re-exports './packs/index.js'. The packs are fixtures (packs/index.ts says so itself); on the public surface they would ship in the app bundle and be importable, which is how a fixture becomes what an app reads when the real pack is late. They follow the convention testing/arbitraries.ts already sets: imported by relative path from a .test.ts, in no barrel. grade.test.ts fails if the export returns.

open_gate_with_no_owner.subject: INV-GRD-28's no-Japanese-tokenizer grep
open_gate_with_no_owner.detail: highlight.test.ts:109 scans packages/core/package.json and packages/core/src/grading/** only — correct for this file lane. The invariant says 'no Japanese tokenizer is linked into the app', so apps/mobile, packages/ui and the root lockfile need the same grep from a task whose lane reaches them.

defects_found_by_the_promised_test.found_by: normalise.test.ts, written because normalise.ts:10 claimed a test that did not exist
defects_found_by_the_promised_test.defect: NFC ran BEFORE format characters were stripped, so stripping one could join a base and a combining mark the format character had kept apart: 'a' + U+200D + U+0301 normalised once to the two-code-point 'á' and twice to the precomposed 'á'.

One pass read the LEFT neighbour from the output being built and the RIGHT neighbour from the input being read. '-一-' came out 'ー一ー' and normalised again to 'ーーー'. Reordering does not fix it: 'アゝ一ア' fails the mirror way round.
defects_found_by_the_promised_test.fix: The three rewrite rules run to a bounded fixed point; the bound is 2 * length + 2 and the convergence argument is in the function's comment.

defects_found_by_the_promised_test.found_by: normalise.test.ts, idempotence of tier1Normalise for the ja fixture pack
defects_found_by_the_promised_test.defect: Whitespace was stripped AFTER the ja fold, so an iteration mark separated from its kana by a space did not expand until a second pass: 'が　ヾ' → 'がヾ' → 'がが'. Reordering does not fix it either — NFKC itself creates whitespace for 52 code points, U+309B and U+309C among them.
defects_found_by_the_promised_test.fix: The four tier-1 stages run to a bounded fixed point, the same pattern as normaliseJa.
